items.quote: Risco relativo de TDAH em mulheres com lipedema: RR=1,424 (IC 95%: 1,2218–1,6598; p<0,0001)
old_statements: Women meeting lipedema screening criteria have a higher prevalence of positive ADHD self-report (ASRS-18) than women without lipedema (76.9% vs 54%; RR 1.424).

items.quote: Broader adipogenic, gut-immune, HLA-associated, cancer-related, ADHD-related, and systemic immunomodulatory concepts are separated into a dedicated exploratory section; they are secondary hypotheses and are not required for the central mast cell-histamine-QST-pain claim.
items.note: The abstract only names 'ADHD-related' concepts as a secondary, exploratory, untested hypothesis and does not report any measured association between lipedema and ADHD, so it is on-topic but not directly informative.

propositions.statement: Self-reported ADHD symptoms are associated with lipedema in women, in unadjusted cross-sectional screening comparisons.
propositions.rationale: The only primary study shows higher positive ADHD screening in women meeting lipedema criteria; reviews only restate it.

evidence.finding: In 354 women, positive ASRS-18 ADHD self-report was 76.9% with lipedema vs 54% without (RR 1.424, 95% CI 1.22-1.66); lipedema screening scores correlated with ADHD scores.
Hypothesis paper cites an ADHD relative risk of 1.42 among lipedema comorbidities.
Perspective review restates ADHD symptom prevalence of 76.9% vs 54% (RR 1.424) in a cohort of 354 women.

dropped.reason: Mentions ADHD-related concepts only as an untested exploratory hypothesis; reports no finding on the association.

verdicts.suggested_statement: Limited evidence suggests self-reported ADHD symptoms are more common in women screening positive for lipedema, based on cross-sectional data.
verdicts.note: Rests on a single cross-sectional screening study (E1); E2 and E3 are correctly marked context and secondary_of E1. The plural 'comparisons' implies more than one study; hedge as limited evidence. E4 correctly dropped.
